chapter: Learning drums and trombone, New Orleans
title: Drumming in Buddy Petit's band and singing Tight Like That
summary: He played about three weeks in Buddy Petit's band on Franklin Street with George Washington, Walter Decou and Big Eye Louis, and sang Tight Like That.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Now, let's see if we can tell about any more of the bands you played with around town here. You mentioned the Decatur Street job that you had with George and Bernard Boyd.
Well, I would say here in town from then, from the Decatur Street job... By the way, I happened to play drums with Buddy Pity a little while. Oh, you didn't?
Not so long. It was the last part of the entertainers. We had a nightclub, yeah, you called entertainers. Oh yeah. It was on Franklin Street, they called it, I guess then. Was it a crows out now?

Right. Right. Well, I played drums in there with him for about three weeks. Who else was in the band looking at? Well, at that time I remember Buddy Pity, a Trombone player called George Washington, was in the band then. He had a piano player in the band,
Walter DeCoult. Well, I knew him. He was a piano at that time.
And I think a clarinet player you called Big Eye Louie. That's all I knew, Big Eye Louie.

I never didn't know his other name. Some people called him Louie Nelson too. His real name was Deleal though, Louie Deleal, but his father had called him Louie Nelson for some reason. I think the big guy told me his father had worked with some people called Nelson when he was a boy. A lot of people just called him Nelson then. But that's one reason Bunker always called Louie Nelson. The trombone is called Dr. Nelson's son because of the other big guy. His name was Well, I never didn't know much about him. In fact, that's all the members I knew then at that time in
Buddy Pity Band. And the time I was in Buddy Pity Band, they had one song around here that I used to sing pretty good in the band. It was a song you called Tight Like That.
Oh yeah, sure. The record came out about that time. Yeah. Well, from then on I ... Louie Armstrong made a record of that too, yeah.
